claim: Hampsfell from Grange-over-Sands is a 3.5-mile (5.6 km) walk with 225 m of ascent, rated easy with uphill sections, about 1.4 hours at standard pace, starting from Grange-over-Sands town centre.
quote: Distance: 3.5 miles (5.6 km) ... Ascent: 225 metres ... A walk along the lanes or quiet roads near the town and superb short grass on the slopes of Hampsfell ... view finder which describes views in all directions

claim: Hampsfell summit is 220 m high above Grange-over-Sands and bears the Hospice, a stone shelter built in 1846 by the vicar of Cartmel with a rooftop viewfinder.
quote: Height: 220m ... viewfinder on top of hospice ... built in 1846 by a Cartmel vicar ... a viewpoint on its roof with a list of sights giving bearings and a viewfinder

claim: A Cartmel village circular taking in Holker Hall and Hampsfell is 7.7 miles (12.4 km) with 315 m ascent, 3-4 hours, starting from Cartmel racecourse.
quote: 7.7 miles (12.4 km) with 315 metres of elevation gain ... approximately 3-4 hours ... begins at Cartmel racecourse ... Holker Hall ... Hampsfell ... Cartmel Priory

claim: Short walks directly from Cartmel village include Holker Hall (3 km, easy, 2 hrs) and Eggerslack Wood (5.6 km, easy, 2 hrs).
quote: Holker Hall ... Distance: 3km | Duration: 2 hours | Difficulty: Easy ... Eggerslack Wood ... Distance: 5.6km | Duration: 2 hours | Difficulty: Easy

claim: Whitbarrow Scar and Lord's Seat circular is 10.9 km (6.7 mi) with 304 m ascent, about 2 hrs 41 min, starting from Mill Side layby off the A590; limestone is slippery when wet.
quote: Distance: 10.9 km (6.7 miles) ... Ascent: 304 m ... 2 hours 41 minutes ... SD451840 near Mill Side ... limestone becomes slippery when wet

claim: The National Trust Arnside Knott circular is 1.7 miles with parking on Knott Lane (LA5 0BP), giving views to the Lakeland fells and Morecambe Bay.
quote: Arnside Knott circular walk ... 1.7 miles ... National Trust car park is located on Knott Lane (postcode: LA5 0BP)

claim: Gummer's How is a short sharp walk of 2.3 km (1.4 mi) with 118 m ascent, around 40 minutes minimum, from the picnic-area car park on the A592, with a small rocky scramble step en route.
quote: Distance: 2.3 km (1.4 miles) ... Ascent: 118 m ... 39 minutes ... SD389876 (Gummer's How picnic area) ... stone pitched steps ... rocky step requiring basic scrambling

claim: The Old Man of Coniston direct route from Walna Scar Road car park is 6 km (3.7 mi) with 600 m of ascent in about 2 hr 12 min, passing the old quarry workings and Low Water tarn.
quote: Distance: 6.0 km (3.7 miles) ... Ascent: 600m ... Minimum 2 hours 12 minutes ... SD289971 on Walna Scar Road ... Low Water ... summit cairn and trig point

claim: The Old Man of Coniston tops out at 2,633 ft / 803 m and is one of the higher Lake District fells, with circular routes around 9.4 km (5.8 mi) and ~550 m gain, moderate to challenging.
quote: At 2,633 feet (803 metres), Coniston Old Man is one of the higher fells in the Lake District ... 9.4km (5.8 miles) ... elevation gain is approximately 550m

claim: Coniston village lies about 18 miles (~29 km) by road from Cartmel, roughly a 27-minute drive — within the 30 km radius.
quote: The driving distance between Cartmel to Coniston is 18 miles, which is approximately 29 kilometers. It takes approximately 27 minutes to drive from Cartmel to Coniston.

claim: Cartmel Fell's high point is Raven's Barrow at 152 m (499 ft), a Wainwright Outlying Fell with a large summit cairn, with short walks from St Anthony's Church (around 1 mile round trip).
quote: Height: 152 metres (499 feet) ... Wainwright Outlying Fells ... identified by the large cairn ... child summit of Gummer's How

claim: A longer Arnside Knott and Heathwaite circular is around 5.8 miles with ~800 ft (240 m) of ascent, taking 2.5-3 hours, rated moderately challenging.
quote: 5.8 mi with an elevation gain of 800 ft and takes about 2.5–3 hr to complete
